header.stance: 油價下降仍難延續漲勢，年底升息風險使美債反轉

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 油價再跌，美債漲勢卻未能延續

荷姆茲海峽可望重新開放，油價再度下跌，美債卻未能延續週四漲勢。美國殖利率起初跟隨歐債下降，之後反轉，2 年期收盤上升 4 個基點至 4.09%，10 年期上升 3 個基點至 4.48%。交易員再次給予 Fed 年底前升息相當高的機率。

消費信心改善、通膨預期下降，仍不足以維持早盤漲勢。股票上漲、波動率下降，高收益債 ETF 穩定，使防禦性債券需求減少。原油降低了再一波能源衝擊的風險，卻沒有消除先前累積的物價壓力或再次緊縮的可能。

海外的對照更鮮明。英國與德國前端因和平消息大幅上漲，ECB 官員卻警告，即使衝突結束，通膨仍可能需要進一步行動。英國產出轉弱、家庭通膨預期升高，讓政策面對不同方向的壓力。信用市場中，Lloyds 支付明顯利差取得日圓資金，印尼基金則因本地債市賣壓演變為流動性問題，延後贖回。

## 前端回吐部分週四漲幅

談判提高荷姆茲航運恢復的希望，布蘭特在歐洲時段一度低於 $86。英國 2 年期殖利率下跌 14 個基點至 4.20%，德國 2 年期下跌近 10 個基點至 2.58%；美國 2 年期也先走低，但未能維持。

至紐約收盤，市場估計 Fed 年底前升息機率約 75%，2027 年 3 月前則完全反映一次升息。35 位經濟學家的調查較不鷹派，中位數預測首次降息在 2027 年 6 月，12 月前再降一次，使目標區間降至 3%–3.25%。兩者都不預期近期寬鬆，但市場更重視最終降息前再升息的風險。

密西根大學初值調查顯示，信心由 44.8 升至 48.9，現況為 48.4、預期為 49.3。1 年期通膨預期由 4.8% 降至 4.6%，長期指標由 3.9% 降至 3.4%。較低預期給政策制定者等待空間，但信心轉強、物價預期仍高，也使持續降通膨尚難確定。

5 年期殖利率上升 3 個基點至 4.21%，30 年期上升 2 個基點至 4.97%。2s10s 縮窄 1 個基點至 39 個基點，2s30s 縮窄 2 個基點至 88 個基點；2s5s10s 蝶式利差下跌 1 個基點至 −15 個基點，2s10s30s 維持 −10 個基點。即使週五反轉，全週 2 年與 5 年期殖利率仍各跌 8 個基點，10 年期跌 7 個基點，30 年期跌 4 個基點。

10 年期實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率分別上升 1 與 2 個基點至 2.17% 與 2.31%。5 年期實質殖利率上升 4 個基點至 1.82%，7 年期上升 2 個基點至 1.98%，20 年與 30 年期則持平至上升 1 個基點。前端與中段變動較大，較符合政策溢價回升，而非獨立的長債衝擊。

雇主薪酬數據也提醒市場成本仍高。3 月非軍職員工的雇主薪酬成本平均每小時 $49.32，其中工資 $33.72、福利 $15.60；私人企業平均為 $46.60。12 月對應總額為 $48.78 與 $46.15。這些是金額水準，不是就業成本指數的成長率，但上升仍與服務業利潤及價格有關。

最短端國庫券並未跟隨附息債下跌。4 週與 6 週債券等值殖利率各降 1 個基點至 3.66% 與 3.67%，8、13、17 與 26 週維持 3.69%、3.71%、3.76% 與 3.80%；52 週上升 1 個基點至 3.86%。眼前現金市場仍平穩，1 年期則保留較晚緊縮的風險。

## 信用需求偏好收益、優先順位與流動性

LQD 小跌 0.06%，HYG 持平，JNK 上漲 0.02%。股票延續反彈，S&P 500 上漲 0.50%、Nasdaq 100 上漲 0.64%、半導體上漲 1.52%；VIX 下跌 9.05% 至 17.68，美元指數下降 0.11% 至 99.75。美債小幅走弱時，公司信用風險承擔意願仍穩。

Lloyds Banking Group 發行 ¥750 億武士債，為兩年來首次在日本國內發行。截至 6 月 12 日，該市場會計年度發行額達 ¥5,030 億，為 2015 年以來同期最高。相對較短天期、利差高於國內替代品，吸引日本買家；部分海外發行人即使加計換匯成本，日圓借款仍具經濟效益。

Lloyds 的 6 年期、5 年後可贖回券種，以交換利率加 78 個基點定價。三井住友銀行 2031 年到期券在 4 月定價為加 28 個基點，S&P 對該日本銀行評等比 Lloyds 高一級。利差差距反映發行人與結構不同，投資人獲得補償，也未阻礙交易完成。

槓桿融資則有潛在新資金供給。銀行為 Triton 收購德國齒輪箱製造商 Flender 安排約 €17 億貸款，預計 6 月下旬行銷。併購融資稀少有利借款人壓低價格，但公開分銷仍需確認需求。Metinvest 處境更困難：烏克蘭鋼鐵商在先前再融資失敗後，用內部現金償還 4 月 $4.28 億到期款，如今研究重返市場；其 2029 年 10 月券在 4 月初殖利率曾高於 12.5%。

貸款曝險內部也在轉移。美國 CLO ETF 今年流入逾 $90 億，去年同期接近 $70 億，同時資金流出上市業務發展公司。較高基準利率支持浮息收入，也增加底層企業負擔。CLO 優先級之下有次順位資本先吸收損失，在民間信貸違約疑慮增加時，受償順位與可交易流動性因而更具吸引力。

SpaceX 首日交易呈現股權風險需求的規模。$750 億發行後，股價以 $150 開出，高於 $135 承銷價，一度達 $163，首日收漲 19%。市場吸收如此大量供給，大盤仍上漲，而大型科技與基建承諾仍持續占用融資能力。

## 歐洲債券上漲，通膨爭論仍在

ECB 最新溝通限制了投資人對和平帶動債市反彈的推演。存款利率升息 25 個基點至 2.25% 後，Peter Kazimir 認為物價壓力擴散，需要進一步行動。5 月通膨為 3.2%，新展望顯示核心通膨至少到 2028 年仍高於目標；市場反映 2026 年再升息一次，2027 年上半年再一次的機率為 70%。

其他官員則偏好先等待。活動疲弱限制連續升息的理由，但產能受損與先前能源成本的延遲影響，也可能使通膨即使在協議後油價快速回落時仍偏高。歐洲前端同時反映緩解機會，以及緩解來不及阻止後續緊縮的風險。

英國 4 月 GDP 月減 0.1%，3 月為增加 0.3%，是 2025 年 8 月以來首次萎縮。服務減少 0.2%，生產持平，營建增加 0.1%；截至 4 月三個月仍成長 0.7%，略快於前一個三個月期間。因此，單月疲弱還不能證明動能崩落。

家庭預期則較不利。英國 1 年期通膨預期中位數由 2 月 3.2% 升至 4.0%，5 年期由 3.7% 升至 3.9%；53% 預期未來一年利率上升，前次為 30%。即使油價較低、月度產出偏弱支持英債，英格蘭銀行仍受到限制。

德國央行預估成長在 2026 年為 0.5%、2027 年 0.8%、2028 年 1.4%，公共支出抵銷部分戰爭衝擊；通膨預估今年 2.9%、2027 年 2.7%、2028 年 1.9%。財政支持強化活動，也可能延緩物價穩定。

波蘭則朝較不緊縮的方向討論。貨幣政策委員 Ireneusz Dabrowski 表示，5 月通膨意外降至 3.1% 後，十人委員會幾乎都降低了對再次升息的擔憂，可能在 2026 年從 3.75% 降息，但這是政策訊號而非決策。匈牙利也因通膨較溫和而討論寬鬆；羅馬尼亞三年高點的通膨支持維持利率，捷克官員則保留升息可能。

週末對澳洲的評估同樣認為，緊縮循環接近尾聲。2026 年已升息三次後，成長與就業走弱、通膨動能減輕，經濟學家預期澳洲央行維持 4.35%。市場對 12 月再升息的反映，由完全計入降至約 60%。長債買家目標是 10 年期殖利率向 4.5% 移動，短端投資人預期最終降息，防禦型帳戶偏好通膨連結債。不同部位的分歧，在於景氣放慢後通膨還會持續多久。

## 日本買家結構與日圓部位增添波動

外資 4 月賣出超長期日債多於買進，為 2024 年以來首次。通膨、財政供給與日銀落後情勢的疑慮，壓過數十年高點殖利率的吸引力。不過，國內買家並未缺席：Iyogin 在 ¥1.7 兆證券投資組合中，4 月開始小額買進超長期券，是十年來首次投資日債。

買家結構改變，使長端更難預測。外國經理人撤出時，區域銀行審慎回流，殖利率提高尚未帶來一致增強的買盤。日本機構在國內外債券間選擇時，避險成本與波動仍和名目利差一樣重要。

週末部位顯示，日圓空單達九年高點，即使日銀升息與匯率支持已大致被反映，美日利差仍支撐套利需求。2024 年意外升息、加速減少購債，曾使匯率與股市部位快速平倉。若日銀超預期，擁擠空單可能再放大日圓升勢與全球去槓桿；若只是符合預期、指引審慎，套利部位則可能維持。

## 本地流動性與財政成本限制新興市場緩解

即使油價與美元下降，EMB 僅上漲 0.09%。印尼顯示，共同利多不一定到達國內市場。資產急跌、印尼盾波動後，政府債券難以出售，兩檔基金延後贖回。據報規模 5.7 兆印尼盾的 KIM Fixed Income Fund Plus，截至週四一週下跌 1.5%；6,914 億印尼盾的伊斯蘭基金下跌 0.7%。

印尼央行減少買債、非例行升息，原本希望透過容許較高殖利率防衛匯率。贖回延後呈現對基金流動性的代價，問題不再只是價格下跌，也包括如何滿足投資人提款。

孟加拉面對的實體限制，可能無法靠全球燃料降價迅速解決。天然氣短缺使 Cumilla 經濟區近 $7.5 億鋼鐵、玻璃與鋁業計畫停滯，平均零售電價上升 17%，5 月通膨達 16 個月高點。能源不足限制新增產能，又提高家庭與企業成本，削弱成長、稅收與競爭力。

印度財政與通膨消息，則使債券面對相反力量。據報當局願在全球情勢需要時，讓赤字最高達 GDP 的 4.8%，而非 4.3% 目標。原油逾 80% 仰賴進口，燃料與肥料補貼壓迫預算；10 年期殖利率一度到 6.91%，之後回到 6.88%，一項估計認為可能增加 3,500 億盧比國庫券借款。

接著公布 5 月 CPI 年增 3.93%，低於預估的 4.02%，也略低於印度央行 4% 目標。數據後，10 年期在 6.89% 保持漲勢。但食品通膨由 4.20% 升至 4.78%，央行也已把會計年度通膨預測由 4.6% 上修至 5.1%。整體數字有利債券，仍未消除食品、匯率與補貼風險。

巴西則高於預期。5 月消費者物價上漲 0.58%，預測中位數 0.53%，年通膨達 4.72%，高於 4.5% 目標上緣。食品飲料上漲 1.33%，其他壓力也超出最直接受戰爭影響的項目。Selic 已為 14.5%，數據降低再寬鬆空間，維持高利息收益的代價是昂貴的國內融資。

委內瑞拉顧問競標出現新的成本比較。Lazard 提出以 $2,500 萬主導估計 $1,500 億至 $2,000 億重整，遠低於 Centerview 討論的至少 $1.5 億安排，後者包括不設上限的 0.1% 成功費與每月 $75 萬。顧問更換與債權人條件都尚未定案，但在債券、貸款、仲裁及其他債權核對前，競爭報價使費用有了議價空間。

雅加達中央移轉款被削減約 15 兆印尼盾、約初始預算 16% 後，繼續研究印尼首檔市政債。債券與擬議財富基金都仍待財政部核准。基建資金可能更分散，但執行仍受監理條件限制，同時移轉減少削弱城市資源。

## 接下來更重要的是執行與 Fed，而非標題

WTI 收跌 3.23% 至 $84.88，布蘭特下跌 3.37% 至 $87.33，黃金卻與美債損益兩平通膨率一同上升，漲 3.05% 至 $4,215。股票歡迎降溫之際，市場仍保留部分保護需求。週五美債反轉顯示，單靠現貨油價更低，已不足以延續前日漲勢。

6 月 12 日截止時間後，巴基斯坦總理表示，美國與伊朗同意立即停止軍事行動、解除美國海軍封鎖，並在 6 月 19 日於瑞士正式簽署。荷姆茲實際通行、未再交火與原油持續較低，將決定這項宣布能否成為持久通膨緩解。受損產能與已進入核心價格的壓力，可能需要更久才能解決。

6 月 15–17 日美國生產、貿易物價與消費數據，最後通往 17 日美東 14:00 FOMC 決策，以及 14:30 Warsh 首次會後記者會。生產與零售穩健、進口物價普遍上漲，或預測傾向升息，都會支持前端政策溢價回升；活動較弱、物價壓力較輕、指引中性，則可能重新打開週四的實質利率緩解空間。

資金日程由 6 月 15 日 $890 億 13 週券與 $770 億 26 週券開始，16 日有 $650 億 6 週券及 $130 億 20 年期增額發行，18 日有 $240 億 5 年期 TIPS 增額發行。6 月 19 日固定收益市場假日縮短反應時間。需求、配售與現金利率將呈現政策預期變化時的承接能力；投標疲弱或資金緊張，則可能對期限溢價增加另一層壓力。

overall_summary.headline: 油價再跌，美債漲勢卻未能延續
overall_summary.session_narrative:
談判提高荷姆茲重開希望，美國殖利率起初跟隨歐洲大幅反彈下降，之後反轉。2 年期上升 4 個基點至 4.09%，10 年期上升 3 個基點至 4.48%；年底升息機率約 75%，2027 年 3 月前則完全反映一次行動。

密西根信心改善至 48.9，短長期通膨預期均降低。原油再跌，實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率卻上升；股票上漲、波動率降低，高收益債 ETF 穩定，防禦性債券需求較少。Lloyds 支付明顯利差進入武士債市場，CLO ETF 流入則偏好優先順位與流動性。

英國產出偏弱仍未消除歐洲通膨疑慮，日本外資賣超與擁擠日圓空單也增加部位風險。印尼基金延後贖回反映本地流動性緊張，印度較溫和 CPI 則與補貼造成的借款壓力拉鋸。截止後宣布美伊停止行動，使協議落實與下週 FOMC 同樣成為焦點。

section_summaries.summary: 密西根通膨預期下降，前端殖利率與政策定價卻回吐早盤緩解，短期現金利率仍平穩。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Treasury Rally Fades Despite Another Drop in Oil

Treasuries failed to extend Thursday's rally even as hopes of reopening the Strait of Hormuz sent oil lower again. US yields initially followed European bonds down, then reversed: the 2-year finished 4 basis points higher at 4.09% and the 10-year rose 3 to 4.48%. Traders again assigned substantial probability to a Fed increase before year-end.

Consumer sentiment improved and inflation expectations eased, but neither was enough to sustain the early move. Equities rose, volatility fell and high-yield funds held steady, leaving less demand for defensive bond positions. Lower crude reduced the risk of another energy shock without removing earlier price pressures or the possibility of renewed policy restraint.

The contrast was sharper overseas. UK and German front ends rallied strongly on the peace headlines, yet ECB officials warned that inflation could require further action even after the conflict ended. Weak UK output and higher household inflation expectations pulled policy in different directions. In credit, Lloyds found yen funding at a visible premium, while Indonesian funds delayed redemptions as a local bond selloff became a liquidity problem.

## The Front End Gives Back Part of Thursday's Gains

Brent briefly traded below $86 in Europe as negotiations raised hopes for Hormuz shipping. UK 2-year yields fell 14 basis points to 4.20% and German 2-year yields dropped nearly 10 to 2.58%. US 2-year yields also started lower, but the move did not last.

By the New York close, traders put the probability of a Fed increase by year-end at roughly 75%, with a move fully priced by March 2027. A 35-economist survey was less hawkish: its median called for the first cut in June 2027 and another by December, taking the target range to 3%–3.25%. Neither view anticipated near-term easing, but markets placed more weight on an increase before any eventual cuts.

The preliminary Michigan survey showed sentiment rising to 48.9 from 44.8, with current conditions at 48.4 and expectations at 49.3. One-year inflation expectations declined to 4.6% from 4.8%, and the long-run measure fell to 3.4% from 3.9%. Lower expected inflation gave policymakers room to wait, while stronger confidence and still-high price expectations made it harder to argue that the disinflation process was secure.

The 5-year yield rose 3 basis points to 4.21% and the 30-year added 2 to 4.97%. The 2s10s spread narrowed 1 basis point to 39; 2s30s narrowed 2 to 88. The 2s5s10s butterfly fell 1 basis point to −15, while 2s10s30s stayed at −10. Despite Friday's reversal, yields were down 8 basis points over the week at two and five years, 7 at ten and 4 at thirty.

Real yields and breakevens both rose at ten years, by 1 and 2 basis points to 2.17% and 2.31%. Five-year real yields increased 4 basis points to 1.82%, seven-year yields rose 2 to 1.98%, and the 20- and 30-year sectors were unchanged to 1 basis point higher. The larger front-end and belly moves fit the return of some policy premium rather than a separate long-bond shock.

Employer compensation data supplied another reminder of cost levels. Civilian compensation averaged $49.32 an hour in March, comprising $33.72 of wages and $15.60 of benefits; private-industry compensation averaged $46.60. December's corresponding totals were $48.78 and $46.15. These are levels, not Employment Cost Index growth rates, but their rise remains relevant to service-sector margins and prices.

The shortest bills did not share the coupon selloff. Four- and six-week coupon-equivalent yields fell 1 basis point to 3.66% and 3.67%. Eight-, 13-, 17- and 26-week yields held at 3.69%, 3.71%, 3.76% and 3.80%; the 52-week added 1 basis point to 3.86%. Immediate cash conditions stayed calm while the one-year sector retained the risk of later policy tightening.

## Credit Demand Favors Yield, Seniority and Liquidity

LQD slipped 0.06%, HYG was unchanged and JNK gained 0.02%. Stocks continued to recover, with the S&P 500 up 0.50%, Nasdaq 100 up 0.64% and semiconductors up 1.52%. VIX fell 9.05% to 17.68, and the dollar index declined 0.11% to 99.75. Corporate risk appetite remained resilient during the mild Treasury loss.

Lloyds Banking Group sold ¥75 billion of Samurai bonds, its first domestic Japanese offering in two years. Fiscal-year market issuance reached ¥503 billion by June 12, the strongest comparable total since 2015. Relatively short maturities and spreads above domestic alternatives attracted Japanese buyers, while yen borrowing remained economical for some foreign issuers after currency swaps.

Lloyds' six-year tranche, callable after five, paid 78 basis points over swaps. A Sumitomo Mitsui Banking note due 2031 had priced at 28 basis points in April, with S&P rating the Japanese bank one notch higher. The spread gap reflected differences in issuer and structure; investors received a concession without preventing execution.

Leveraged finance had prospective new-money supply. Banks arranged about €1.7 billion of loans for Triton's purchase of German gearbox maker Flender, with marketing due in late June. Scarcity of acquisition financing was helping borrowers compress pricing, though general syndication still needed to establish demand. Metinvest's position was more difficult: the Ukrainian steelmaker explored returning to markets after internal cash repaid a $428 million April maturity when earlier refinancing plans failed. Its October 2029 bond had yielded more than 12.5% in early April.

Investors were also shifting within loan exposure. US CLO ETF inflows exceeded $9 billion for the year, versus nearly $7 billion in the comparable 2025 period, while money left publicly traded business-development companies. High base rates support floating-rate income but also burden the underlying borrowers. Senior CLO tranches have subordinated capital beneath them to absorb losses first, making payment priority and tradable liquidity attractive as private-credit default concerns grow.

The SpaceX debut showed the scale of appetite for equity risk. After a $75 billion offering, shares opened at $150 against a $135 offer price, reached $163 and ended their first day 19% higher. The market absorbed that volume while broader indexes advanced, even as large technology and infrastructure commitments continued to draw on financing capacity.

## Europe Rallies, but the Inflation Debate Persists

The ECB's latest communication limited how far investors could extrapolate the peace-driven bond rally. Following the quarter-point deposit-rate increase to 2.25%, Peter Kazimir argued that spreading price pressures would require further action. May inflation was 3.2%, and the revised outlook kept core inflation above target through at least 2028. Markets priced one more increase in 2026 and a 70% chance of another in the first half of 2027.

Other officials favored waiting after the latest move. Weak activity constrained the case for a sequence, while damaged production capacity and lagged energy costs could keep inflation elevated even if an agreement brought crude down quickly. European front-end yields reflected both the possibility of relief and the risk that it would arrive too late to avoid further tightening.

UK GDP fell 0.1% in April after March's 0.3% gain, the first contraction since August 2025. Services declined 0.2%, production was flat and construction rose 0.1%. The three months through April still grew 0.7%, slightly faster than the preceding three-month period, so the weak latest month did not establish a collapse in momentum.

Household expectations were less favorable. Median one-year UK inflation expectations rose to 4.0% from 3.2% in February, and the five-year measure increased to 3.9% from 3.7%. Some 53% expected interest rates to rise over the next year, compared with 30% previously. That left the Bank of England constrained even as cheaper oil and weak monthly output supported gilts.

The Bundesbank projected German growth of 0.5% in 2026, 0.8% in 2027 and 1.4% in 2028 as public spending cushioned the war shock. Inflation was expected at 2.9% this year, 2.7% in 2027 and 1.9% in 2028. Fiscal support strengthens activity but may also slow the return to price stability.

Poland was moving toward a less restrictive discussion. MPC member Ireneusz Dabrowski said concern about another increase had receded across nearly all of the ten-member council after May inflation unexpectedly slowed to 3.1%. That opened a possible route to a 2026 cut from 3.75%, though it was a policy signal rather than a decision. Softer inflation also encouraged easing debate in Hungary; Romania's three-year-high inflation argued for a hold, while Czech officials retained the possibility of an increase.

Weekend Australian assessments similarly placed the tightening cycle near its limit. Economists expected the RBA to hold at 4.35% after three 2026 increases, with weaker growth and employment and easing inflation momentum. Market odds of another December increase fell from fully priced to about 60%. Long-bond buyers targeted a move in 10-year yields toward 4.5%, short-end investors anticipated eventual cuts and defensive accounts favored inflation-linked debt. The positions differed on how much inflation would outlast the slowdown.

## Japan's Buyer Base and Yen Positioning Add Volatility

Foreign investors sold more super-long JGBs than they bought in April for the first time since 2024. Inflation, fiscal supply and concern that the BOJ was behind the curve outweighed multi-decade-high yields. Domestic buyers were not absent: Iyogin began small super-long purchases in April, its first JGB investment in a decade, within a ¥1.7 trillion securities portfolio.

That change in the buyer mix leaves the long end less predictable. Foreign managers were withdrawing as a regional bank cautiously returned; higher yields alone had not produced a uniformly stronger bid. For Japanese institutions choosing between domestic and overseas debt, hedging costs and volatility remain important alongside the nominal yield gap.

Weekend positioning showed yen shorts at a nine-year high, sustained by the US-Japan rate differential even with a BOJ increase and currency support substantially priced. In 2024, a surprise increase and faster reduction in bond buying triggered a rapid unwind across currencies and equities. Crowded shorts could again amplify a yen rally and global deleveraging if the BOJ exceeded expectations. An anticipated move with cautious guidance could instead leave carry positions intact.

## Local Liquidity and Fiscal Costs Limit EM Relief

EMB gained only 0.09% despite lower oil and a softer dollar. Indonesia showed why the common relief need not reach domestic markets. Two bond funds delayed redemptions as selling government debt became difficult after the asset rout and rupiah volatility. The KIM Fixed Income Fund Plus, reported at 5.7 trillion rupiah, fell 1.5% in the week through Thursday; a 691.4 billion-rupiah sharia fund declined 0.7%.

Bank Indonesia's retreat from bond buying and off-cycle increase sought to defend the currency by allowing yields to rise. Redemption extensions showed the consequence for fund liquidity: losses were no longer only a question of market prices, but of meeting investor withdrawals.

Bangladesh faced a physical constraint that cheaper global fuel might not quickly solve. Gas shortages stranded almost $750 million of steel, glass and aluminum projects in the Cumilla economic zone. Average retail power tariffs rose 17%, and May inflation reached a 16-month high. Unavailable energy restricts new productive capacity while raising costs for households and businesses, weakening growth, tax receipts and competitiveness.

India's fiscal and inflation news pulled bonds in opposite directions. Authorities were reported willing to let the deficit reach as much as 4.8% of GDP rather than the 4.3% target if global conditions required it. With more than 80% of crude imported, fuel and fertilizer subsidies were pressuring the budget. The 10-year yield briefly reached 6.91% before returning to 6.88%; one estimate put possible extra bill borrowing at 350 billion rupees.

May CPI then came in at 3.93% year on year, below the 4.02% consensus and just under the RBI's 4% target. The 10-year retained gains at 6.89% after the release. Food inflation accelerated to 4.78% from 4.20%, however, and the RBI had already raised its fiscal-year inflation forecast to 5.1% from 4.6%. The headline helped bonds without removing food, currency and subsidy risks.

Brazil received an upside surprise. May consumer prices rose 0.58% against a 0.53% median estimate, taking annual inflation to 4.72%, above the 4.5% upper target limit. Food and beverages rose 1.33%, with broader pressure beyond the most war-sensitive components. At a 14.5% Selic rate, the result reduced room for further easing and maintained high carry at the cost of expensive domestic finance.

Venezuela's advisory contest produced a new cost comparison. Lazard offered to oversee the estimated $150 billion–$200 billion restructuring for $25 million, well below the at-least $150 million arrangement discussed with Centerview, including an uncapped 0.1% success fee and $750,000 monthly retainer. Neither an adviser replacement nor creditor terms had been finalized. The competing offer made fees contestable before bond, loan, arbitration and other claims were reconciled.

Jakarta continued examining Indonesia's first municipal bond after central-government transfers were cut by roughly 15 trillion rupiah, about 16% of its initial budget. Finance Ministry approval remained outstanding for both the bond and a proposed wealth fund. Infrastructure funding could become more diversified, but execution still depended on regulation while the transfer loss weakened the city's resources.

## Implementation and the Fed Now Matter More Than Headlines

WTI ended 3.23% lower at $84.88 and Brent fell 3.37% to $87.33, but gold rose 3.05% to $4,215 alongside higher Treasury breakevens. The moves left some demand for protection even as stocks welcomed de-escalation. Friday's US bond reversal showed that cheaper spot oil alone was no longer sufficient to extend the earlier rally.

After the June 12 cutoff, Pakistan's prime minister said the US and Iran had agreed to an immediate cessation of military operations, removal of the US naval blockade and a formal signing in Switzerland on June 19. Actual passage through Hormuz, an absence of renewed attacks and sustained lower crude will determine whether that announcement becomes durable inflation relief. Damaged supply capacity and pressure already in core prices may take longer to resolve.

US production, trade-price and consumption releases on June 15–17 culminate in the FOMC decision June 17 at 14:00 ET and Warsh's first post-meeting press conference at 14:30. Firm production and retail sales, broad import-price gains or projections favoring an increase would support renewed front-end policy premium. Softer activity, less price pressure and neutral guidance would reopen the real-yield relief seen Thursday.

The funding calendar starts June 15 with $89 billion of 13-week and $77 billion of 26-week bills. June 16 brings $65 billion of six-week bills and a $13 billion 20-year reopening, followed June 18 by a $24 billion five-year TIPS reopening. The June 19 fixed-income holiday shortens the reaction window. Demand, bidder allocations and cash rates will show whether balance sheets can absorb the supply while policy expectations shift; weak bidding or funding strain would add a separate source of pressure to term yields.

US yields initially followed a strong European rally as negotiations raised hopes of reopening Hormuz. They then reversed: the 2-year rose 4 basis points to 4.09% and the 10-year added 3 to 4.48%. Traders put year-end hike odds near 75%, with a move fully priced by March 2027.

Michigan sentiment improved to 48.9 and both short- and long-run inflation expectations eased. Oil fell again, yet real yields and breakevens rose. Stocks gained, volatility declined and high-yield funds were stable, leaving less support from defensive bond demand. Lloyds accessed Japan's Samurai market at a visible spread premium, while CLO ETF inflows favored seniority and liquidity.

European inflation concerns persisted despite weak UK output; Japanese foreign selling and crowded yen shorts added positioning risks. Indonesia's fund redemption delays showed local liquidity strain, while India's softer CPI competed with subsidy-driven borrowing pressure. A post-cutoff announcement of US-Iran cessation now puts implementation alongside next week's FOMC at the center of the outlook.
